use /lib
use /ui
from /scope/settings-window import SettingsWindowScope
from /scope/user-preferences import UserPreferencesScope
from /ui/components/theme-editor import ThemeEditorScope
from /ui/theme import ThemeScope

export ui-component RibbonApplicationTabScope:
    concept: {RibbonApplicationTabConcept}

concept RibbonApplicationTabConcept:
    pitch:
        The ribbon's Application tab: the commands for the application itself,
        rather than the project.

    shape: {RibbonApplicationTabShape}

shape RibbonApplicationTabShape:
    description:
        The Application tab of the ribbon, last of the tabs.

    groups:
        appearance:
            An "Appearance" group holds the Brightness command, its one
            control; there is no Dark mode switch, since the slider reaches
            both modes.

        colours:
            A "Colours" group, between Appearance and Preferences, holds the
            Theme command.

        preferences:
            A "Preferences" group holds the Settings command.

    commands:
        brightness:
            A "Brightness" slider, which runs the whole interface from its
            darkest to its lightest: a moon icon, then a horizontal slider
            120 pixels wide, then a sun icon, with nothing showing the setting
            as a number. As a ribbon setting, it has no background of its
            own, and sits straight on the commands' area, as tall as a slim
            button. Its tooltip says it makes the whole interface darker or
            lighter, from its darkest to its lightest, keeping its contrast,
            and that double-clicking it resets it.

            Its one track runs through every appearance the @{ThemeScope}
            allows, darkest first: dark mode from its darkest brightness to
            its lightest, then light mode from its darkest to its lightest,
            one position for each step, with no switch between them. So all
            the way left is dark mode at its darkest, and all the way right
            light mode at its lightest; dragging past dark mode's lightest
            step changes the window to light mode, and back.

            Dragging it changes the mode and the brightness straight away as
            it moves, and once it is let go saves the mode showing and each
            mode's brightness among the @{UserPreferencesScope}. A mode that
            can't be saved shows a notification titled
            "Could not save brightness", with why; a brightness that can't be
            saved fails quietly. Its thumb follows the appearance showing,
            however that was changed, such as from the palette, but not while
            it is being dragged.

            Double-clicking anywhere on it, its icons or its track, puts the
            mode showing back to its brightness at 0, keeping the mode, and
            saves it; the second click doesn't also move the thumb.

            It is primary, so the collapsed ribbon keeps it: its icons and
            track as they are, only as wide as they are, as tall as a small
            button.

        theme:
            A "Theme" button with a palette icon. Clicking it opens the
            @{ThemeEditorScope}. Its tooltip says it chooses the base colour,
            and the colours of Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask.

            It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon
            leaves it out.

        settings:
            A "Settings" button with a gear icon. Clicking it opens the
            @{SettingsWindowScope}, where the system prompt each chat tab sends
            is edited. Its tooltip says so, and gives its keyboard shortcut,
            Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS).

            It is primary, and a full button.

content.text:
There's now a "Reset Brightness" button directly below the Brightness slider on the ribbon's Application tab. Clicking it does the same as double-clicking the slider: it puts the current mode's brightness back to 0, keeps you in the same mode, and saves the setting.

A new test (`reset_brightness_sits_beneath_the_slider`) checks that the button sits under the slider and that clicking it resets brightness without changing the mode. All the ribbon tests pass. The full suite now has 4 failures, all from the code-to-spec and spec-reading prompt files not matching their tests, as before. The answer-selection test that failed last time passed on this run.

Some choices the spec didn't settle, for you to confirm:
- **Look:** it's a slim button with a rotate-arrow icon, sharing the slider's column in the Appearance group.
- **Disabled when there's nothing to reset:** it's greyed out while brightness is already at 0, with a tooltip saying so. That follows the ribbon's rule that a command which can't run is disabled.
- **Not in the collapsed ribbon:** it isn't marked primary, so the collapsed ribbon leaves it out. There, double-clicking the slider still resets brightness.

The code is in `src/ribbon/application_tab.rs` and `src/ribbon/mod.rs`, and the test is in `src/main_window.rs`. The spec (`spec/ui/components/ribbon/application-tab/index.pi`) doesn't describe this button yet, so it needs a Spec pass to catch up.
